dossier_meta.statement_text: Assuming only that each $a_i \neq 0$, what geometric constraints can be imposed on a set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ which imply non-trivial uniform upper bounds on $\Pr(X \in S)$?
dossier_meta.context_text: The paper introduces a new generalisation of the Littlewood–Offord problem to $\mathbb{R}^d$ in which no assumption is made on the sizes of the nonzero vectors $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, only that they are nonzero. The authors observe that this makes the question much more about the geometry of $S$ than about spatial anti-concentration of $X = a_1\xi_1 + \cdots + a_n\xi_n$, giving it a very different flavour from previous Littlewood–Offord variants.
